message.content:
In Texas, tenants have a number of statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and ensure safe, habitable living conditions. Below is an overview of key rights you should know: | Category | Tenant Right | Key Points | |----------|--------------|------------| | **Security Deposit** | **Limited Use & Return** | • Landlords may hold up to one month’s rent as a security deposit (or two months for furnished units).
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear and tear. | | **Habitability** | **Safe & Functional Living Space** | • Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, and pest control.
• Must provide working smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors. | | **Repair & Maintenance** | **Right to Request Repairs** | • Tenants can request repairs; landlords must respond promptly.
• If landlord fails to repair, tenants may withhold rent or pursue a “repair‑and‑deduct” remedy (though this is limited in Texas). | | **Rent Payment** | **No Unlawful Rent Increases** | • Landlords cannot increase rent during a fixed lease term unless specified in the lease.
• For month‑to‑month leases, landlords must give at least 30 days’ notice before raising rent. | | **Notice Requirements** | **Proper Notice for Entry & Termination** | • Landlords must give 24‑hour written notice before entering the unit (except emergencies).
• For month‑to‑month tenancy, either party must give 30 days’ written notice to terminate. | | **Privacy** | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlords cannot interfere with your right to privacy or disturb your peaceful enjoyment of the premises. | | **Discrimination** | **Fair Housing Protections** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or other protected classes under federal Fair Housing Act and Texas statutes. | | **Lease Terms** | **Enforceable Agreements** | • Written lease agreements are enforceable; oral agreements are also valid but harder to prove.
• Lease terms must comply with Texas law (e.g., no illegal clauses). | | **Eviction Process** | **Legal Eviction Procedure** | • Landlords must follow proper legal steps: serve a written notice (usually 3 days for nonpayment, 30 days for lease termination), file a lawsuit if necessary, and obtain a court order.
• Self‑eviction or “no‑court” eviction is illegal. | | **Tenant Remedies** | **Legal Recourse** | • If landlord violates your rights, you can file a complaint with the Texas Attorney General’s Office, seek mediation, or sue in small claims court. | ### Practical Steps to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, receipts, and photos of any damage or maintenance issues. 2. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Understand the terms regarding rent, deposits, maintenance responsibilities, and notice periods. 3. **Know the Law** – Familiarize yourself with the Texas Property Code sections relevant to residential tenancies (e.g., §§ 92.001–92.021). 4. **Use Written Notices** – Whenever possible, send notices via certified mail or email with read receipts to create a paper trail. 5. **Seek Legal Advice** – If you face disputes, consult a tenant‑rights attorney or local legal aid organization. --- #### Quick Reference: Texas Property Code Sections - **§ 92.001** – Security Deposits - **§ 92.002** – Habitability - **§ 92.003** – Repair & Maintenance - **§ 92.004** – Rent Increases - **§ 92.005** – Notice Requirements - **§ 92.006** – Privacy & Quiet Enjoyment - **§ 92.007** – Discrimination - **§ 92.008** – Lease Enforcement - **§ 92.009** – Eviction Process If you need more detailed guidance or help drafting a lease or notice, let me know!
